key_insight: Hodge–de Rham PINNs represent solutions through decomposed 1-forms to address topological obstructions that can defeat conventional scalar-potential PINNs.
engineering_relevance: This approach could improve physics-informed modeling on domains with holes or singularities where circulation and path dependence matter.
method: Parameterize a 1-form using the Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs decomposition for manifolds with boundary.
Train with an associated PDE loss and connect the learned form to scalar solutions through integral operators.
Use exhaustion functions when the loss integrability condition is not met.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and experiments including the Aharonov–Bohm effect, inexact forms, and nontrivial harmonic and coexact components, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: The operator connecting 1-form and scalar formulations may require problem-specific integration or analysis, complicating implementation.
paper_title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
